* ESMA gives EU crypto firms [three months](https://www.chooserich.live/story/esma-non-mica-stablecoins-exit-p7fufqg) to exit non-MiCA-compliant stablecoins

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Risk-off mood rules the tape: bitcoin briefly sank to a three-week low on Iran jitters, high yields and heavy ETF outflows. Meanwhile, regulators from the EU to Thailand keep reshaping crypto's rulebook. 📉 Bitcoin Slips to Three-Week Low as Iran Jitters Trigger $1B Liquidation Flush Bitcoin dropped below $81,000 to a nearly three-week low as oil climbed on Iran strike fears and elevated Treasury yields weighed on risk assets, triggering roughly $1 billion in crypto liquidations, with ether positions hit hardest. BTC has since steadied near $82,500 after President Trump ruled out an Iran strike before the U.S. midterms. Read full story ⚖️ EU Gives Crypto Platforms Three Months to Drop Non-MiCA Stablecoins The European Securities and Markets Authority has given MiCA-authorized crypto platforms three months to stop offering stablecoins that lack MiCA authorization, a group that includes Tether's USDT and PayPal's PYUSD. Platforms must block new access to these tokens, while national regulators oversee existing customer holdings. More details 💸 Bitcoin and Ether ETF Outflows Swell Toward $1B in October Bitcoin and ether ETF outflows for October are swelling toward $1 billion. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shed about $485 million on Wednesday, their worst day since June, and another $244 million on Thursday, while XRP ETFs were the only crypto funds to post inflows. Read more 🏛️ U.S. Government Moves $1B in Seized Bitfinex Bitcoin A government-controlled wallet holding bitcoin seized from the 2016 Bitfinex hack moved 12,267 BTC, worth roughly $1 billion, in a single transaction on Thursday. The coins went to a new, unlabeled address rather than an exchange, so there is no sign of a sale yet, but traders are watching closely after other seized coins reached Coinbase Prime a day earlier. See details 🌏 Thailand Finalizes Bitcoin and Ether ETF Rules, Effective Oct. 16 Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission has finalized rules for bitcoin and ether exchange-traded funds, with the framework set to take effect on October 16. The move paves the way for regulated ETF access to the two largest cryptocurrencies in Thailand.
